card.name: Software descriptions of what a program does
card.fires_on: Small linking words (to, and, the, they) inside a description of what a software tool or program does, just before the next action verb such as find, load, print or generate. Seen in computing and tech text, not drug labels.

modes.label: Infinitive 'to' after a tool
modes.description: The word 'to' introduces the job a program performs.
modes.example: Google, Yahoo! and Microsoft, use crawlers<< to>> find pages for their algorithmic search results

modes.label: 'and' joining two actions
modes.description: The word 'and' links a second action a program carries out.
modes.example: cat (1) - concatenate files<< and>> print on the standard output

modes.label: Partway through tool names or commands
modes.description: The marked piece falls inside a software term or command listing.

card.writes: It seems to boost words about making or creating things and to suppress 'final' words, so it favors a creation-type verb coming next.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in descriptions of what a computer program does, right before the action it performs.
